sections.h2: Where is the Washington County Register of Deeds in Plymouth?
sections.html:
The Washington County Register of Deeds is at 120 Adams Street in Plymouth, with a mailing address of P.O. Box 1007, Plymouth, NC 27962. The county page lists office hours of 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., Monday through Friday, the office phone as (252) 793-2325 and the fax as (252) 793-6982.

The register is an elected office with a four-year term, according to the county's own page. Its stated purpose is to let the owner of an interest in property give public notice of that ownership, which also protects later buyers from unknown transactions and secret liens. The same office issues birth, death and marriage certificates and marriage licenses.

Washington County is in northeastern North Carolina. The county says it is bisected by US 64 and lies about 120 miles east of Raleigh, 80 miles west of Nags Head and under 50 miles from Greenville. Its three towns are Plymouth, Roper and Creswell, and it borders the Albemarle Sound on the Roper side.

sections.h2: How far back do Washington County land records go?
sections.html:
Land records go back to 1799, when Washington County was formed from Tyrrell County. Marriage records start in 1851, and the actual licenses on file begin in 1881.

Old land grants, deeds, deeds of trust, maps, leases, agreements and powers of attorney all sit in the office. For a seller with a family farm or waterfront parcel, a long chain of title is normal here, and an attorney's title search usually runs through those older books. The office also posts a link to search deeds online.

State birth and death registration started in 1913. The county says it holds some earlier births that were delayed registrations filed after that year. Requests for older vital records should be made in writing with names and dates.

sections.h2: What do you need to record a deed in Washington County?
sections.html:
Two local steps come before recording. The county says every deed must first go to the GIS (mapping) department to get a parcel identifier number, and it must also go to the Washington County tax collector for certification that no delinquent taxes are due.

The alternative to the tax collector's certification is a statement in the deed from the closing attorney that any delinquent taxes will be paid to the tax collector from the closing proceeds. Most closings use that statement.

  • Put the preparer's name on the first page of a deed or deed of trust.
  • Use 8.5 by 11 or 8.5 by 14 inch paper, with a three inch blank top margin on page one and quarter inch margins elsewhere.
  • Print in black on white in a font no smaller than 9 points, one side of the page only.
  • State the type of instrument at the top of the first page.

A document that does not meet those standards can still be recorded, but the register collects the $25.00 non-standard document fee on top of the regular fee. The county also notes that cancellations and satisfactions can now be e-recorded through Simplifile.

sections.h2: What are the recording fees in Washington County?
sections.html:
A deed or general instrument costs $26.00 for the first 15 pages and $4.00 for each additional page, and a deed of trust costs $64.00 for the first 35 pages and $4.00 per extra page. These match the uniform schedule in G.S. 161-10.

Washington County register of deeds charges as the county page prints them

Maps need the GIS department to assign a parcel number and the county review officer to approve them, unless the plat carries one of the standard statements that it creates no new street, shows an existing structure or natural feature, or is a control survey.

sections.h2: Who pays the excise tax when a Washington County house sells?
sections.html:
The seller pays it. The statute says the transferor must pay the excise tax to the register of deeds before the deed is recorded, at one dollar for each $500 or fractional part of the consideration or value of the interest conveyed.

The county page prints the same rate. Half of the proceeds stay with the county and half go to the state, as G.S. 105-228.30 lays out. The settlement statement from the closing attorney will show the stamp amount, so the number does not have to be worked out in advance.

If a deed has no ordinary sale price, ask the register how the stamp applies before you bring it in.

sections.h2: Does the Washington County office record contracts for deed and other seller documents?
sections.html:
Yes, any instrument that affects land can be presented for recording. A seller-financed sale is the common example. Under Chapter 47H, a contract for deed on a one to four family home must be written, signed and acknowledged, and the seller must record the contract or a memorandum of it within five business days.

The buyer under such a contract can cancel until midnight of the third business day after signing. If the seller later tries to forfeit the contract, a written default notice must give a cure date at least 30 days after service.

Other documents a Washington County seller might bring in:

  • A power of attorney, when someone signs the deed for the owner.
  • A recorded map or plat, following the 18 by 24 inch rule and the GIS review.
  • A lease or agreement, which the county lists among its record types.

The county's preparer-name rule means the person who drafted a deed must be named on its first page, so line up the drafter before you go to the counter.

sections.h2: What else should a Washington County seller know about recording?
sections.html:
Recording order matters. Under G.S. 47-18, a conveyance is not valid against lien creditors or purchasers for value until it is registered in the county where the land lies. Registration time decides priority.

  • Call the register at (252) 793-2325 if a deed carries more than 20 names to index.
  • Ask the county tax collector about open tax bills before closing, since the deed needs that certification or the attorney's statement.
  • Ask the closing attorney whether any lien from an older loan still needs a recorded satisfaction.

Waterfront and farm parcels often carry surveys, and any plat that goes with the sale follows the map requirements above.

sections.h2: Can I sell a Washington County house with title or tax problems?
sections.html:
Yes. Unpaid taxes and liens are normally cleared from the sale proceeds by the closing attorney, and a buyer can purchase a house in its current condition. The register's index is the first place a title searcher looks, so start there.

If you want to compare a listing with a cash offer for a Washington County house, you can ask for a written offer on this site.

faqs.q: Is there a fee to record a satisfaction in Washington County?
faqs.a: No. The county lists cancellations and certificates of satisfaction as no charge, and the non-standard document fee does not apply to any cancellation.

faqs.q: Do I need a parcel number before recording a deed in Washington County?
faqs.a: Yes. The county requires every deed to go to the GIS department for a parcel identifier number before it is recorded.

faqs.q: What does a certified birth, death or marriage copy cost at the Washington County Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: The county prints $10.00 for a certified copy and 25 cents for an uncertified one. Certified copies go only to the applicant or immediate family, and fax requests are not accepted.

faqs.q: How long is a Washington County marriage license valid?
faqs.a: Sixty days, and it costs $60.00. The county asks applicants to arrive before 4:30 p.m. because the process takes 15 to 20 minutes.

faqs.q: Who do I call about recording a Washington County deed?
faqs.a: Call the register of deeds at (252) 793-2325. The office is at 120 Adams Street in Plymouth and is open 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., Monday through Friday.
